Be brief. ‘Diary language’ has some typical features such as subjectless sentences (Got up late in the morning), sentence fragments without subjects or verbs (…too bad, boring, not good), contracted forms (they’re, I’ve, can’t, didn’t, etc.), and everyday expressions which people use in speech. Remember not to use such language in more formal kinds of writing.

items.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
items.stem: What do these statements tell you about Anne Frank as a person ? (i) We don’t seem to be able to get any closer, and that’s the problem. May be it’s my fault that we don’t confide in each other. (ii) I don’t want to jot down the facts in this diary the way most people would, but I want the diary to be my friend. (iii) Margot went to Holland in December, and I followed in February, when I was plunked down on the table as a birthday present for Margot. (iv) If you ask me, there are so many dummies that about a quarter of the class should be kept back, but teachers are the most unpredictable creatures on earth. (v) Anyone could ramble on you and leave big spaces between the words, but the trick was to come up with convincing arguments to prove the necessity of talking.
items.answer: To Anne as a person these statements have different meanings. (i) The first statement speaks the importance of having the need of a real friend. (ii) The second statement speaks of Anne’s conviction of considering the diary as her real friend. (iii) The third statement shows her profound love for her elder sister. (iv) The fourth statement is about teachers. She forms an opinion that these are unpredictable. (v) The last statement points out her skill in writing an essay. Thus Anne was a skilled girl having the decent qualities of mind, body and soul. Thinking About Language

items.answer: 2015 Anne and her classmates thought that teachers were the most unpredictable creatures as nobody would know what there was in their minds and what their next step would be.

items.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
items.stem: What does Anne tell about her father?
items.answer: 2014 Anne says that her father is the most adorable man. He married at the age of thirty-six. At that time her mother Edith was twenty-five. Due to Nazi’s occupation, he emigrated to Holland in 1933.

items.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
items.stem: Write down Anne’s rapport with school teachers.
items.answer: 2013 There were nine teachers in school. Among them there were two women and seven males. One Mr. Keesing was an old fashioned type of teacher. He was a strict fellow. He remained angry with Anne because of her talkative habits.

items.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
items.stem: Why was Mr. Keesing annoyed with Anne and what extra homework did he give to her after several warnings?
items.answer: 2009, 2008 Mr. Keesing was annoyed with Anne because she talked too much. In spite of giving her several warnings she continued to talk excessively. After this Mr. Keesing assigned her extra homework, to write an essay on the subject - ‘A Chatterbox’

items.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
items.stem: What arguments did Anne give in her essay titled ‘A Chatterbox’?
items.answer: 2006 In her essay ‘A Chatterbox’ Anne argued that talking was a student’s trait and that the only thing she could do was to try and control it. But she further argued that her trying to manage her talking would not be very effective because her mother talked as much as she did. Therefore, nothing could it be done about an inherited trait.

items.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
items.stem: Express your views on the title of the poem, ‘The Ball Poem’.
items.answer: 2010 When one reads the title ‘The Ball Poem’, one assumes that the poem may be a light-hearted one, perhaps about the joys of childhood. But on the contrary, it talks about how we must not feel disheartened, dejected and desperate about some loss in life but try to stand up and bear the loss through self-understanding.

items.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
items.stem: “Money is external”. What does the poet mean by this expression taken from ‘The Ball Poem’?
items.answer: 2009 By this expression the poet intends to make us realize the mere material value of money which in no way helps us to understand the essential worth of a commodity. In this world of possessions, the value of money is only to buy things and this does not make us understand the true value of things.

items.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
items.stem: ‘He is learning, well behind his desperate eyes’. What is the boy learning from the loss of the ball?
items.answer: 2009 The boy is learning the epistemology of loss from the loss of the ball. He is understanding what it means to lose something he greatly admires.

items.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
items.stem: No use to say ‘O there are other balls’: What do the words in inverted commas mean? Why does the poet think that it is useless to give this suggestion to the boy?
items.answer: 2008 The words in the inverted commas try to suggest that the loss of the ball is not that significant. The poet thinks that it is useless to give this suggestion to the boy as the boy has lost his priceless possession.

items.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
items.stem: ‘An ultimate shaking grief fixes the boy’. Who is the boy? What is his state of mind? Why is he in such a state of mind?
items.answer: 2008 The boy is playing with the ball. He is in the state of grief, sadness and disappointment. His ball has fallen down into the water which can’t be retrieved.

items.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
items.stem: What is the theme of the poem- ‘The Ball Poem’?
items.answer: 2007 In this world, sometimes we lose things which we love and are deeply attached to. We must not feel dejected and lament the loss. We must face the loss with positivity and anticipation of gains in the future. The boy in the poem who lost the ball he loved, was trying to learn to accept his loss and move ahead in life .

items.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
items.stem: What does show that the ball was valuable for the boy?
items.answer: 2005 The ball was valuable for the boy is obvious from the way he reacts after losing it, he was under shock, remained fixed, trembled with grief staring at the place where the ball had fallen. All this shows that he loved the ball and it was valuable for him. Long Answer Type Questions

items.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
items.stem: You have been chosen to address the school assembly, to speak on the epistemology of loss and the resilience of the human spirit during times of crisis. Prepare the speech draft, with reference to the commonality of themes in The Ball Poem’ by John Ber ryman and ‘From the Diary of Anne Frank’. You may begin this way : Good morning everyone. Today, I’d like to discuss two pieces of literature that offer a powerful insight into how to deal with loss and the resilience of the human spirit required during times of crisis. You may end this way : To conclude, I’d like to say that _____ Thank you.
items.answer: 2024 Good morning everyone! Today, I’d like to discuss two pieces of literature that offer a powerful insight into how to deal with loss and the resilience of the human spirit required during times of crisis. In “The Ball Poem” by John Berryman and the excerpt from Anne Frank’s diary, we see a common theme of loss and its impact on individuals. In Berryman’s poem, a young boy is shown struggling after losing his ball. Comparably, during the turbulent years of World War II, Anne Frank writes in her diary about her feelings of loss and loneliness. These works impart lessons about the struggles of life and the importance of resilience in the face of challenges. To conclude, I’d like to say that these pieces of literature serve as poignant reminders of our capacity to grow from the challenges that life throws at us rather than giving up. Thank you.
